discovery.summary: New admin-only engagement page plus first-touch signup-source capture. Read-only queries over existing tables for the funnel, and one additive migration on the users table for the source columns.
non_goals: No third-party analytics service (Plausible, Fathom, Umami, Google Analytics). Separate decision for Chris: costs money, needs his account.

SUPERSEDED 2026-08-13 by Chris: the original non-goal was "no anonymous visitor-ID cookie". Chris chose full attribution, which means first-touch capture DOES set a session cookie on every anonymous visitor where none is set today. Recorded in spec D3 with its consequences.
No cookie-consent banner. Chris decision D3 creates the need for one in the EU; solving it is a separate piece of work and explicitly not in this feature.
No append-only event log. Admin match-deletes and handle-resets therefore make a past funnel non-reproducible; documented as a known limit in spec D7.
No cohort retention grid. At 10-20 users it would be noise.
No changes to the existing /admin/reports turn-timing page.
acceptance_criteria: Admin-only page at /admin/engagement, in the Platform admin submenu, returning 403 for a non-admin.
Funnel is strictly nested; a test asserts the sequence never increases, including a dataset where a user archived their agent.

Funnel steps follow the product gate ladder (handle then agent then connection), NOT connection before agent. A test asserts a user who built an agent but never connected is counted at built-an-agent.
Step membership is ever-did-X: archived agents and deleted connections still count.
Bots and internal users are excluded everywhere via the stored users.is_internal flag, applied by one shared filter.
is_internal is set at all three user-creation sites (Google sign-in, bots seating, dev login), not only by the migration backfill.
First touch survives later navigation and the Google OAuth round trip; an end-to-end test proves it.
First touch is cleared on sign-out so a second user in the same browser does not inherit it.
Users created through the two MCP sign-in callers record source "mcp", never "direct".
Played-a-turn excludes was_defaulted rows; a test with a no-show player proves it.
Every people-count is COUNT(DISTINCT users.id); a test with one user owning three agents and many player rows proves it counts once.
Came-back-another-day uses the page window timezone, not UTC; a test with a US evening session spanning two UTC days proves it is not a return visit.
Smoke-test matches (TEST_NAME_PREFIX) are excluded, matching the existing /admin/reports filter.
Source table shows source, signups, and how many played. A row with no capture renders as "unknown", kept separate from a genuine "direct" visit.
Stuck-people list labels users who have no handle, and caps at 50 rows with a remainder count.
Funnel starts at signed up = 100 percent, shows no anonymous visitor count, and carries a note saying visitor numbers arrive when an analytics tool is added.
Migration is additive and reversible, uses op.batch_alter_table for constraint operations, and leaves existing users with NULL source columns.

admin/users/{id} can toggle is_internal, renders that control for floor-admin targets (outside the not-floor_admin gate), and audit-logs it via a new AdminAction value; admin/users shows an internal column.
First-touch capture is advisory: a failure logs and continues and never breaks a page render.

checklist.goal: Give platform admins one page showing where new users fall out of the signup-to-playing journey, and which traffic source each signup came from, so the next week of work targets the biggest measured leak instead of a hunch.
checklist.audience: Platform admins only, behind require_platform_admin. Not public and not shown to normal users. Chris is the only regular reader today, so at 10-20 users named rows matter more than percentages.
checklist.constraints: Async routes and async DB calls only. Dev DB is SQLite, prod is Postgres, so any constraint operation in the migration must use op.batch_alter_table. Migration must be additive and reversible; existing users get NULL source. No third-party analytics service and no anonymous visitor cookie, so no cookie-consent banner is introduced. Follow the existing app/read_models/admin_reports.py pattern for the query module and the existing admin page conventions in app/routes/admin_web.py.
checklist.silent_risk_note: A wrong funnel still renders a clean page. Already hit this concretely: counting each step independently made the funnel go UP in the middle (11 users had connected an AI but 13 had joined a match) because users who archived an agent dropped out of one step but not the next. Source capture has the same shape - the UTM tag is gone from the URL by the time the user clicks sign in, and the Google OAuth round trip drops query params, so a naive implementation silently records NULL for every signup, passes tests, and looks fine in prod.
checklist.design_settled_note: Page layout is settled from the design conversation (four summary numbers, nested funnel, stuck-people list, source table). The capture half is NOT settled: whether first touch is recorded in middleware or at the login route, how it survives the Google OAuth redirect, what string counts as a source, and how crawler traffic is excluded are all open questions.
checklist.completeness_risk_note: The signup-source value threads through first-touch capture, the session, sync_google_user, a users-table migration, the read model, and the template. Separately the bot-vs-agent and admin/test-account exclusion filter must be applied identically in every count on the page, or the four summary numbers will contradict the funnel below them.
